---
title: Anthropic
description: anthropic() — Claude provider via @anthropic-ai/sdk. Lazy-loaded peer-dep; install when you use it.
---

> The Anthropic SDK is the production path for Claude. agentfootprint's `anthropic()` factory wraps it as an `LLMProvider` — same interface as `mock()`, so the rest of your agent code is identical between dev and prod.

## Install

```bash
npm install @anthropic-ai/sdk
```

The SDK is a peer dependency declared in `peerDependenciesMeta` with `optional: true` — npm doesn't auto-install it. Lazy-required at first call; friendly install hint if missing.

`anthropic()` is imported from the `agentfootprint/providers` subpath, NOT the main `agentfootprint` barrel. Every provider lives there — `mock`, the browser variants and `createProvider` included — so bundlers walking the main entry never touch the optional peer-dep requires. (The one provider helper on the main barrel is `providerFromEnv`.)

## Use

```ts
import { Agent } from 'agentfootprint';
import { anthropic } from 'agentfootprint/providers';

const provider = anthropic({
  apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY!,
  // defaultModel: 'claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929',  // optional, used when Agent doesn't override
});

const agent = Agent.create({
  provider,
  model: 'claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929',
}).build();
```

Model ids are Anthropic's own: dateless from the 4.6 generation on (`claude-opus-5-5`), dated before it (`claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`, or its alias `claude-sonnet-4-5`).

## Tools (native function calling)

Anthropic's Messages API has native tool_use blocks. The provider translates the agent's `Tool[]` into the API's tool format and round-trips assistant tool_calls via `LLMMessage.toolCalls`. ReAct correctness preserved across multi-iteration runs.

### One tool per reply — `parallelToolCalls: false`

By default Claude may ask for several tools **at once**: one assistant message carries many `tool_use` blocks, and the agent runs them all inside a single loop iteration. That is usually what you want — it is faster and cheaper.

It is not what you want when the **shape** of the loop is part of what you are measuring. Per-iteration analysis reads one tool source per iteration: `localizeContextBug` seeds one `'tool'` suspect from that iteration's `lastToolResult`, and `removableSources` de-duplicates by tool name. So a reply that batched three tools is attributed to the **last** tool of the batch — the other two never appear as their own influence rows, and you cannot ablate them individually.

Set `parallelToolCalls: false` to cap the model at one tool per reply:

```ts
const provider = anthropic({
  apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY!,
  parallelToolCalls: false, // one tool per reply → one tool per iteration
});
```

On the wire this sends `tool_choice: { type: 'auto', disable_parallel_tool_use: true }`. `auto` is deliberate: the model still decides **which** tool to call, and whether to call one at all — only the *count* is capped. Nothing is sent on requests that carry no tools (Anthropic rejects `tool_choice` there), and `parallelToolCalls: true` sends nothing either, because allowing batches is already Anthropic's default.

Asking for this in the system prompt ("call one tool at a time") is **not** equivalent — that is a request the model may ignore, this is a request parameter the API enforces. Cost: one extra round trip per tool.

The same option exists on `browserAnthropic()`, and both adapters put the identical field on the wire.

## Thinking

`.thinking({ budget })` asks the model to think before it answers. Claude models disagree about how that is asked — a budget sent to Claude 4.7 or later is an HTTP 400 — so the provider sends the shape **the model** takes:

| Model | On the wire |
|---|---|
| Opus 4.7 and later, Sonnet 5 and 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable, Mythos 5 and 5.1, Mythos Preview — and any id not listed here | `thinking: { type: 'adaptive', display: 'summarized' }`, no budget |
| Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 (they take both; budget deprecated, still accepted); Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.1, Opus 4, Sonnet 4, Sonnet 3.7 | `thinking: { type: 'enabled', budget_tokens: budget }` |
| Claude 3.5 Sonnet, 3.5 Haiku, 3 Opus, 3 Sonnet, 3 Haiku | refused at `build()` — they cannot think |

<CodeFile path="examples/features/96-thinking-per-model.ts" region="per-model" title="examples/features/96-thinking-per-model.ts (region: per-model)" />

**Adaptive thinking takes no budget.** The model decides whether and how much to think, so the budget is not sent (dev mode says so once per model) and no effort level is guessed from it. It still keeps `max_tokens` above itself — `budget + 1024` when the request's is lower — because thinking counts toward `max_tokens`. `display: 'summarized'` is what makes the thinking readable; these models otherwise return it empty.

**Refused before anything is sent**, as an `UnsupportedThinkingError` (from `agentfootprint/providers`; `provider`, `model`, `reason`, `retryable: false`):

- `'no-thinking'` — at `build()` for the agent's model and its skill and escalation brains; on the first call for a model `.configure()` picks at run time.
- `'budget'` — a budget model takes a whole number of at least 1024.
- `'temperature'` — thinking takes only the default temperature, 1.
- `'forced-tool-choice'` — `.outputSchema(…, { strategy: 'tool-forced' })` cannot ride with a budget; use `'instruct'` (or, on Opus 4.6 or Sonnet 4.6, declare them adaptive — below).

`withRetry` does not retry the refusal, `withFallback` does not move it to the other side, and `withCircuitBreaker` does not count it: the request is wrong, not the vendor.

<CodeFile path="examples/features/96-thinking-per-model.ts" region="refused" title="examples/features/96-thinking-per-model.ts (region: refused)" />

`browserAnthropic()` and `invokeModelGateway()` read the same table, and platform ids (`us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0`, `claude-opus-4-5@20251101`) count from `claude-` on. Ask what will be sent with `provider.thinkingMode(model)`, a `ThinkingMode`: `'adaptive'`, `'budget'` or `'none'`. Wrappers forward it; `withFallback` sends each side its own model's shape and answers the least of the two, so a fallback that cannot think is refused at build. Source: Anthropic's [thinking support by model](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking-troubleshooting).

**An id the table cannot read** — a gateway alias, an application-inference-profile ARN, a deployment name — is read as adaptive. If it serves a model that needs a budget (Claude 4.5 and earlier), say so with the adapter's `thinkingMode` option; return `undefined` for the table's answer. The same option makes Opus 4.6 adaptive, which in budget mode does not think between tool calls. The provider declares the result and sends it, so the build check and the wire agree:

```ts
invokeModelGateway({ /* … */ model: 'haiku-fast', thinkingMode: (id) => (id === 'haiku-fast' ? 'budget' : undefined) });
```

## Forced tool choice is model-specific

`carriesForcedToolChoice` still says whether the adapter writes a forced
choice on its wire. `forcedToolChoiceFor(provider, model)` also reads the
optional `supportsForcedToolChoice(model)` restriction.

Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 reject forced tool choice,
with or without a thinking request. Haiku 5.5 accepts it. The SDK, browser and
InvokeModel gateway adapters use one model table and refuse an unsupported
choice before sending anything, with `UnsupportedToolChoiceError` from
`agentfootprint/providers` (`provider`, `model`, `retryable: false`).
This follows Anthropic's [forced-tool compatibility rules](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking#response-prefill-and-forced-tool-use).

<CodeFile path="examples/features/96-thinking-per-model.ts" region="forced-choice" title="Check the model before forcing a tool" />

An explicit `.outputSchema(…, { strategy: 'tool-forced' })` refuses at run
start when the provider/model does not support it. Choose `'instruct'`
explicitly if prompt-based output fits your use case. The internal constrained
classifier already has a strict text-parsing path and uses that path for these
models; it does not weaken its allowed-value check.

Wrappers preserve the declaration; a fallback pair requires support on both
sides. The default resilience policies do not retry this refusal, switch
providers or count it as a circuit failure. Custom policies remain yours.
Unknown deployment aliases keep their previous behavior: the table does not
claim to know the model hidden behind them, and the service may still refuse.
The thinking-mode option controls only thinking, not forced-tool support.

## Thinking replay: stop only when unsafe

During a tool turn, Anthropic requires the preceding assistant content,
including signed and redacted thinking, in its original order. A tool result
does not finish that turn. Earlier completed turns can omit thinking; see the
[tool-workflow contract](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking-tool-workflows).

The SDK, browser and InvokeModel gateway share one replay check at the adapter
that actually sends the call. If saved evidence proves that required active-turn
thinking was changed, removed or reintroduced, the call raises
`UnsafeThinkingReplayError` from `agentfootprint/providers` before sending.
Keep system instructions, tools and earlier messages stable until the turn
finishes; retain the original assistant blocks. Default resilience wrappers do
not retry or hide this refusal. Unknown local provenance is not proof that an
opaque signature is invalid; server authentication remains the server's job.

For a witnessed completed turn, eligible invalid thinking is removed explicitly.
`agentfootprint.agent.thinking_omitted` records every removed block's indices,
reason, provider and model, with `phase: 'prepared'`: it proves preparation,
not delivery or acceptance. No reasoning or signature appears in this event.
The run persists retirement into its history so saving and resuming cannot
silently bring those blocks back. Standalone provider callers can use
`onReplayPrepared`; successful responses also carry `replayOmissions`.

`LLMMessage.replay` holds optional JSON layout and consistency evidence, not a
copy of the signed content. Preserve it alongside `thinkingBlocks` when managing
history yourself. Complete and streaming replies retain the same block order;
a no-thinking `end_turn` reply also records completion. The receipt stays at the
provider-port boundary; `servedAt` reports a `thinking-replay` gap when a later
adapter omission means it cannot prove the downstream message body.

For a standalone integration, import the replay types from
`agentfootprint/providers`. `MessageReplay` describes the saved evidence;
each `ReplayPart` identifies a text span, thinking block or tool call in its
ordered layout. A layout marked `lossy` is negative evidence, not a promise of
recoverable content. `ReplayPreparation` is the pre-transport hook payload:
the prepared request plus its omissions. Each `ThinkingReplayOmission` names
one removed block without its contents, and `ThinkingReplayReason` describes
the locally observed inconsistency. These types do not authenticate signatures
or prove that a prepared request was sent.

Only documented bound model families get the local prefix check. Older models,
unknown aliases and cross-model signature compatibility are not guessed. No
preserved-thinking beta or server drop policy is enabled. Prefix and contiguous
sequence rules follow Anthropic's
[preserved-thinking documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking).

## Streaming

`provider.stream(req)` uses the SDK's native iterator; chunks land as they arrive. Final chunk carries the full `LLMResponse` (toolCalls + usage + stopReason) — single round-trip serves UI tokens AND ReAct decisioning.

## Production patterns

Wrap with resilience decorators for production:

```ts
import { withRetry, withFallback } from 'agentfootprint/resilience';
import { anthropic, openai } from 'agentfootprint/providers';

const provider = withRetry(
  withFallback(
    anthropic({ apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY! }),
    openai({ apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY! }),
  ),
  { maxAttempts: 5 },
);
```

See [Resilience guide](doc:resilience).

## Browser variant

For browser environments where the Anthropic Node SDK doesn't bundle cleanly, use `BrowserAnthropicProvider` — `fetch`-based, zero peer deps. Requires the `anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access: true` header (which the provider sets automatically). Production browser apps should proxy through a backend.

## Limitations

- Multi-modal content (images, video) not supported — `LLMMessage.content` is `string`.
- `responseFormat` (JSON-Schema-coerced output) not exposed yet — pass schema instructions via `systemPrompt`.
